info.title: Price to Profit API
info.summary: Quotes, pricing, invoices and profit for hair extension stylists.
info.description:
Backend for **Price to Profit**, the quote, pricing and invoice app for hair
extension stylists.

A stylist builds a quote from hair (bought in packs and sold by the gram with a
markup), labour hours, services, materials and fees. The API prices it, keeps
the history, turns accepted quotes into invoices and renders branded PDFs. It
also shows the stylist what they really earn: cost, profit and profit per hour.

## How to read this API

* **Base path**: every business endpoint lives under `/v1`.
* **Auth**: `POST /v1/auth/register` with **email**, **name** and
  **password**, then `POST /v1/auth/verify-otp`. **No token is issued
  until** `POST /v1/auth/login` with email and password. Send
  `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` afterwards. Public: health,
  `GET /v1/app-config`, register, verify-otp, resend-otp, login and refresh.
* **Which business**: `POST /v1/businesses` creates a studio for the
  signed-in account. `X-Business-Id` is only required when that account
  owns more than one studio.
* **Money** is exact. Send amounts as strings or numbers with up to two
  decimals (`"350.00"` or `350`). Amounts in responses are **strings** such as
  `"2104.00"` so no precision is lost.
* **Dates** are `YYYY-MM-DD`; timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC.
* **Lists** are paginated with `limit` (1-100, default 20) and `offset`, and
  return `{items, total, limit, offset}`.
* **Partial updates** use `PATCH`: only the fields you send change.
* **Errors** always look like this:

```json
{"error": {"code": "not_found", "message": "Quote 42 was not found."}}
```

| code | HTTP | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `validation_error` | 422 | The body or query is malformed (see `details`). |
| `business_rule_violation` | 422 | Valid input that breaks a rule. |
| `pricing_error` | 422 | A value the pricing engine cannot work with. |
| `unauthorized` | 401 | Missing or invalid Bearer token. |
| `not_found` | 404 | The record does not exist. |
| `conflict` | 409 | Not allowed in the record's current state. |
| `file_too_large` / `unsupported_file_type` | 413 / 415 | Logo upload problems. |

## Typical flow

1. `POST /v1/auth/register` → `POST /v1/auth/verify-otp` →
   `POST /v1/auth/login`, then `POST /v1/businesses` on first launch.
2. `POST /v1/library` to save hair products, services and materials.
3. `POST /v1/quotes/preview` while the stylist edits, for live totals.
4. `POST /v1/quotes` to save, `PATCH /v1/quotes/{id}/status` as it progresses.
5. `GET /v1/quotes/{id}/pdf` to share with the client.
6. `POST /v1/quotes/{id}/invoice`, then `PATCH /v1/invoices/{id}/status` as
   payments arrive.

## Scope

There is **no subscription** handling in this version. Email delivery of
OTPs is not wired yet: in `local` the OTP is returned in the register
response so you can verify without a mailer.

get.description: Returns 200 while the process is running. Touches nothing else.
Returns 200 when the database answers a simple query.
Read on every app launch. Tells the app whether it must update (`minimum_app_version`), whether maintenance mode is on, and where to send users for support, terms and privacy.

post.description:
Create an account with **email**, **name** and **password**. A 6-digit OTP is issued to verify the email. **No session token** is returned; call `POST /v1/auth/verify-otp`, then `POST /v1/auth/login`.

If `PTP_ENVIRONMENT` is `local`, the OTP is included in the response so you can finish signup without sending email.

Saves a reusable product or service. Which pricing fields are required depends on `kind`:

| kind | required | optional |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hair` | `grams_per_pack`, `pack_price` | `markup_percent` |
| `labour` | - | `hourly_rate` |
| `service`, `material`, `fee` | `unit_price` | `unit_cost`, `unit_label` |

Pricing fields that do not apply to the kind are ignored.

Runs the full pricing engine and returns every line's price and cost plus the totals. Nothing is saved. The quote builder calls this as the stylist types, so the totals bar updates live.

The example request is the worked example from the spec. It returns subtotal **2,005.00**, VAT **99.00**, total **2,104.00**, balance **1,504.00**, profit **1,240.00** and **354.29** per hour.

patch.description:
Moves the quote through its lifecycle:

| from | allowed targets |
| --- | --- |
| `draft` | `sent`, `accepted`, `declined` |
| `sent` | `draft`, `accepted`, `declined` |
| `accepted` | `sent`, `declined` |
| `declined` | `draft`, `sent` |
| `invoiced` | none (locked) |

A quote becomes `invoiced` only through **Create an invoice**. Sending the current status is a no-op.

get.description:
Everything the app home screen shows:

- **period**: quotes created, quoted value, win rate, invoices issued, money collected, profit and profit per hour for the date range (default: this month so far).
- **outstanding**: money still owed on unpaid invoices.
- **quote_status_counts** / **invoice_status_counts**: all-time counts.
- **recent_quotes**: the five newest quotes.

Profit figures count invoiced quotes by invoice issue date, so a quote's profit is counted once, when it is billed.

QuoteLineInput.title: QuoteLineInput
QuoteLineInput.description:
One line of a quote, as sent by the app.

Values are resolved in this order: the value on the line, then the
library item (`library_item_id`), then the business defaults.

| kind | required | defaults |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hair` | `grams_required`, `grams_per_pack`, `pack_price` | `markup_percent`, `whole_packs` from the business |
| `labour` | `hours` | `hourly_rate` from the business |
| `service`, `material`, `fee` | `unit_price` | `quantity` = 1, `unit_cost` = 0 |

Allowed: draft -> sent/accepted/declined, sent -> draft/accepted/declined,
accepted -> sent/declined, declined -> draft/sent. A quote becomes
`invoiced` only by creating its invoice.
